claims.text: The precursor alloy is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
A metallic and hydride powder blend can undergo in-situ alloying during additive manufacturing and subsequent sintering.
An ultra-high vacuum below 10^-7 Pa is required for the proposed sintering process.
Adding 2-5 wt% reactive Ti powder provides an effective oxygen getter.
TaH0.5, NbH, HfH2, TiH2, and ZrH2 decompose completely in the proposed 400-600°C stage.
The decomposition temperatures of the listed hydrides correlate with their hydride formation enthalpies.
Heating to approximately 1200-1300°C homogenizes the HfNbTaTiZr alloy.
A cooling rate above 100°C/s is sufficient to retain the high-temperature phase.
The Ti getter forms TiO2 and minor Ti-H-O complexes that sequester oxygen.
Dissolved oxygen stabilizes alpha-HCP phases in HfNbTaTiZr, and oxygen sequestration prevents their nucleation.
Getter Ti reacts preferentially with oxygen because it has a higher oxygen affinity than Hf, Nb, Ta, Zr, and matrix Ti.
The ultra-high-vacuum environment drives complete decomposition of all five hydride precursors.
Complete dehydrogenation enables formation of a clean BCC solid solution.
Rapid quenching suppresses diffusional formation of alpha-BCC or ordered phases and traps metastable beta-BCC.
Getter-free or insufficient-vacuum processing causes oxygen-derived TiOx or TiO precipitation.
Getter-free or insufficient-vacuum processing stabilizes alpha-HCP phases in HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed process produces greater than 99% relative density.
Rapidly quenched material consists of a single metastable beta-BCC phase.
The rapidly quenched alloy has a grain size below 5 µm.
The final alloy contains less than 50 ppm oxygen.

contradictions.description: Ti powder is described as an added getter and is predicted to form TiO2 and Ti-H-O products, yet the final microstructure is described as single-phase with negligible oxygen and no oxide precipitates. The hypothesis does not clarify whether the getter is external to the specimen or how its reaction products are removed.

The alloy is specified as equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr while 2-5 wt% additional Ti powder is introduced, but it is not stated whether that Ti remains external. If incorporated, the processed alloy would no longer be equiatomic.
